maria (Support): flagging a customer stream hang in prod. Python SDK generator just stops yielding after a few partial tokens when run over HTTP/2 via httpx. connection stays open, no exception. repro steps attached.

emma (Customer): repro we ran: redwood-py 0.9.4, httpx 0.24.0, python 3.10.7. behavior: streaming yields a couple of partial-token deltas then nothing. curl --http2 to the same endpoint returns a complete stream. here's the simplified output capture we see (raw lines from capture):

```
data: {"delta":"Hel"}
data: {"delta":"lo"}
data: {"delta":" , wor"}
data: {"delta":"ld"}
event: keepalive
data:
```

emma (Customer): with httpx the last keepalive line and the following data sometimes get merged into one frame and our generator never yields the final combined piece. curl+nghttp shows separate events.

jonah (SDK): thanks for the detail. can you also paste the minimal client snippet you used? suspect SSE parser waiting for a final newline / strict delimiter logic that doesn't tolerate http2 frame coalescing + empty-data keepalive.

emma (Customer): minimal client below:

```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)
with client.stream("/v1/streams/generate") as gen:
    for chunk in gen:
        print(chunk)
```

emma (Customer): we also tried async httpx with `AsyncClient(http2=True)` and saw same. switching http2 off made it reliable.

maria (Support): repro steps I documented: 1) pip install redwood==0.9.4 httpx==0.24.0 2) run capture.py (attached) 3) observe generator yield stops after partials, connection open 4) tcpdump shows server still sending events but SDK parser doesn't emit final token.

li-wei (Eng-ML): pinging eng-runtime, this smells like our SSE parser being strict about an event frame that contains only a colon/heartbeat then an immediate data line with no intervening newline. http/2 can coalesce frames which means we might see `:keepalive\ndata: {...}` in one read. older parser expected `\n` boundaries.

jonah (SDK): temporary workaround: create httpx client with `http2=False` or run redwood-py with the new relaxed parser flag (added in 0.10.1). example: `client = RedwoodClient(..., stream_opts={"sse_strict": False})` — not ideal but works for customers on older httpx.

jonah (SDK): root cause: strict SSE parsing + keepalive colon-only events + http2 frame coalescing produced a partial-state where parser waited for next `\n` before emitting. fixed in SDK v0.10.1 by treating a following `data:` token as terminating the keepalive state.

maria (Support): proposed next steps: 1) ask customer to upgrade to redwood-py 0.10.1 (we patched parser) 2) if they can't upgrade, use `http2=False` in httpx as a workaround 3) collect full tcpdump and SDK debug logs if issue persists so eng-runtime can verify.

emma (Customer): trying upgrade now, will report back. thanks. :pray:

ops-bot: support ticket #78912 created and linked to this thread.

jonah (SDK): tagging follow-up: if upgrade doesn't fix it, we'll add a guard in the generator to flush on EOF/timeouts and escalate to eng-runtime. please include `--capture-raw` logs when you reply.

maria (Support): assigning to @jonah to follow up with the customer. closing interim loop once they confirm upgrade fixed it.

emma (Customer): upgrade to 0.10.1 fixed it for us. generator now yields full tokens over http2. thanks team! :tada:
